one_line: Indo-Greek ambassador of King Antialcidas who dedicates the Garuda pillar to Vasudeva at Besnagar.

appearance.age_look: early 30s, lean but athletic build, about average height with the wiry toughness of a seasoned traveller
appearance.face: Oval face with a straight nose, high cheekbones and a defined jaw; light olive complexion tanned slightly darker by the Indian sun; short neatly trimmed beard and moustache; expressive dark eyes with a focused, thoughtful gaze and a default expression of calm diplomatic seriousness with a hint of curiosity.
appearance.hair: Short wavy dark brown hair, cut above the neck and combed back from the forehead, with a narrow dark red cloth fillet (headband) tied around the head, the knot and short loose ends resting behind the right ear.
appearance.costume: A knee-length sleeved chiton of undyed off‑white linen, belted at the natural waist with a plain dark brown leather belt, worn under a medium‑length Greek himation cloak in a muted dusty‑blue wool draped over the left shoulder and wrapping around the body; simple fitted braccae-style light tan cloth trousers peep under the chiton hem for riding practicality (reflecting his long journey to central India); sturdy dark brown leather sandals with ankle straps; over this, a finely woven Indian-style sash in deep maroon cotton with a subtle golden-yellow border is diagonally slung from right shoulder to left hip like a diplomatic badge, its ends neatly tucked; small but clear Indo-Greek jewellery: a single plain bronze ring on his right hand, a modest bronze bangle on his left wrist, and tiny simple bronze stud earrings; the overall look balances Hellenistic ambassadorial dress with subtle adaptation to Shunga-era India while remaining fully modest and practical for courtly appearances.
appearance.signature: A carefully carved handheld wooden Garuda-standard staff about his own height, in polished dark brown wood, topped with a stylised Garuda emblem (eagle-like bird) painted in muted gold and maroon, with a thin saffron ribbon tied just below the finial, which he carries upright as both devotional symbol and diplomatic offering.

ref_desc: Heliodorus of Taxila is a light-olive, short-bearded Indo-Greek man in an off-white chiton, dusty-blue himation cloak, light tan trousers, maroon Indian sash, dark brown sandals, short wavy dark-brown hair with a red headband, and a tall dark-wood Garuda-standard staff with gold-and-maroon finial and saffron ribbon.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character model sheet of Heliodorus of Taxila: an early-30s Indo-Greek man with an oval, light-olive face, straight nose, high cheekbones, short neatly trimmed beard and moustache, and short wavy dark-brown hair held by a narrow dark red cloth headband tied behind his right ear, his dark eyes calm and serious; dress him in a modest knee-length off-white linen chiton with sleeves, belted with a dark brown leather belt, over light tan fitted cloth trousers visible under the hem, and a medium-length dusty-blue wool himation cloak draped over his left shoulder and wrapped around his body, with a deep maroon Indian cotton sash with a subtle golden-yellow border worn diagonally from right shoulder to left hip; add sturdy dark brown leather sandals with ankle straps, a plain bronze ring on his right hand, a bronze bangle on his left wrist, and tiny bronze stud earrings; place in his right hand a tall polished dark-wood staff topped with a stylised eagle-like Garuda finial painted in muted gold and maroon, with a thin saffron ribbon tied just below the finial, and ensure the dominant colours are off-white, dusty blue, maroon, dark brown and muted gold, shown clearly from multiple angles for consistent redrawing.
